findings: Recomputed terminal scores for the 14 required controls are 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.75, 0, 0.25, 0, 0.25, 0, 0, 0, 0, and 0.75. Controls 5 and 14 cannot reach their declared 1.0: CLEAR requires every robot rigid link in R to remain at least 30 mm from F, which includes the bench. The pinned YAM link set includes each arm's base, and both bases are placed at TABLE_HEIGHT on the tabletop, so their surface separation from the bench is not 30 mm. Restrict clearance to the grippers/moving arm links versus the task work area, consistent with selected.json.

The score can be gamed without demonstrating retained stop function. A released window excludes robot/tool contact only with S and N73, so the robot may hold or directly move the jaws; cycle qualification observes only jaw-angle crossings and never requires cold-lever/piston actuation. After C3, L is not revoked by a wrong final open angle and CLEAR does not require the jaws to remain released, settled, and within ±3 degrees. Require externally released stop endpoints, native lever/piston-linked cycles without direct robot/tool jaw driving, and the final angle tolerance throughout the one-second clearance dwell.

The fixture-displacement hard-failure control is not physically executable as specified: F explicitly contains an anchored fixture frame, cover, and bench, yet the control requires fixture translation over 10 mm. A static anchored body cannot produce that event through normal robot actions, and an after-initialization state write is forbidden. Specify a finite, physically breakable fixture mount and its datum, or replace this control with a physically realizable loss event without weakening damage handling.

Several score-critical terms remain ambiguous: “open settled endpoint,” “released settled endpoint,” “adjustment motion occurs,” and “endpoint range” lack complete numeric predicates. In particular, undefined adjustment motion can revoke L on arbitrary numerical jitter, while g73<=0.5 mm has no lower bound and therefore accepts substantial nut/seat penetration until the separate 2 mm damage threshold. Define stop-contact/release and settling observables, a motion threshold with units, the exact endpoint set used for range, and a tight signed seating interval.

selected.json says angle credit is revoked whenever locking prerequisites fail, but contract.json deliberately awards 0.25 for an unseated locking nut in the angle-only and wrong-seating controls. Resolve this contradiction explicitly while preserving meaningful partial credit.

Timing and freshness are otherwise internally consistent: 4800 actions at 20 Hz equal 240 seconds; 240 Hz uses 12 substeps/action and 480 Hz refinement uses 24; the 60-, 48-, and 240-sample windows equal 0.25, 0.20, and 1.00 seconds; action 4800 completes before current-score evaluation; no post-timeout progress or bonus exists. The restored runtime preflight and pinned sources support the 20 Hz configuration path and pre/post physics callbacks, while correctly reserving contact, force, joint-state, and refinement certification for later native probes.

The prior contact-manifold and energized-motion specification failures are repaired: contact force, penetration, and work are now point-wise with explicit pair aggregation/event reset rules, and energized axial motion uses fresh consecutive substep displacement. Industrial evidence also supports the unpressurized closed-position adjustment, nuts 73 and 74, locking with nut 73, and subsequent actuation test; the cold lever, counterholding law, target, and tolerances are properly disclosed as benchmark assumptions.
